title: CUDA IPC handoff latency — customer escalation investigation
content:
Summary:

Short description: On 2026-04-11 between 13:10–13:45 UTC two enterprise customers (acme-fin and streamly) reported large increases in tail latency for text-generation requests served from Dedicated pools in us-west-2. p95 increased from ~120ms to 600–900ms and p99 peaked at ~1.8s. Error rate remained low; throughput unchanged.

Impact: Customer-facing SLO breaches for dedicated customers (monthly SLO: p99 < 800ms). Two escalations raised to SE and SRE teams; customer-initiated throttles and fallback to hosted API for critical traffic.

Observed anomalous signal (high level):
- p50 ~ stable, p95/p99 elevated
- host GPU utilization steady (~70%), CPU utilization increased on the model runner process that coordinates IPC
- queues showed increased wait time between request completion and next kernel launch
- short bursts of GPU page fault activity correlated with tail spikes

Hypothesis (initial): A cross-process handoff path that uses CUDA IPC handles was occasionally serializing access and incurring CPU-side synchronization + page migration, causing disproportionate tail latency.

Timeline (abridged):
- 2026-04-11 13:08 UTC: Internal alert fires for p99 on dedicated-us-west-2 pool (alert: infra-p99-latency-high).
- 13:10: Incoming customer report from acme-fin via support channel; SE escalates to eng-serving-runtime.
- 13:20: Observed matching traces in tracing service (trace ids shared with customer troubleshooting).
- 13:35: Quick mitigation: temporarily re-routed half of acme-fin traffic to a compatible model variant on a different pool (reduced visible p99 for that customer but not others).
- 13:50: Team begins profiling reproducer on a Canary node with capturing nsys traces and bpftrace snapshots.
- 14:30: Root cause hypothesis validated by profiling evidence (see below).
- 16:00: Hotfix candidate prepared and deployed behind a canary switch (disable CUDA IPC handoff; force single-process GPU allocator path).
- 17:45: Canary shows p99 improvement; gradual rollout started.
- 2026-04-12: Post-rollout validation and customer RCA draft sent.

Root cause analysis (detailed):
1) Architectural context: Our multi-tenant model runner can shard a large model across multiple processes for isolation and throughput. When cross-process requests need to hand off a warmed KV cache or attention state, we use CUDA IPC handles to share device memory between processes to avoid expensive host roundtrips. This IPC path relies on fast GPU page mappings and CUDA transport layer (DRM/GDR) to be low-latency.

2) Trigger condition: On certain memory alignment boundaries (observed with the GPT-XXX-32k variants at sequence lengths > 1024) the driver triggered a GPU page migration path that results in the first access to a recently-shared page causing a page-fault-like event. These events are normally rare but were amplified by a micro-burst of concurrent handoffs during a small window of traffic skew.

3) Amplifier: Our IPC handoff code performs a short busy-wait + futex-based synchronization on the CPU side while waiting for the receiving process to ack the mapping. When page migration happened, the receive-side process spent ~10–50ms in kernel/driver code servicing the mapping, which prolonged the CPU busy-wait and blocked the outgoing process from proceeding to the kernel launch. Because several handoffs overlapped, tail latency multiplied.

4) Secondary contributor: A recent change in the per-node cgroups and rlimits (PR #1279) tightened max open file descriptors for user processes to 4096. That reduced the number of concurrent IPC handles we could open before falling back to a serialized path. In practice, when the handle limit was reached we fell back to a slow host-copy codepath (which increased CPU and delayed the GPU kernel readiness even further).

Evidence:
- nsys timeline (canary-03, 2026-04-11 14:10): clear gap between host CPU spin and kernel launch; GPU time slice not the bottleneck.
- dmesg on affected node: repeated lines indicating "NVRM: GPU page migration triggered for address 0x7f..." correlated with p99 windows.
- perf + uprobes: showed futex contention inside ipc_sync_wait() with stacks pointing to ipc_handle_ack() in the model runner binary.
- cgroups metric: number_of_ipc_handles saw spikes and then truncated at 4096 concurrently; trace IDs included in linked artifacts.
- load reproducer: using seq lengths 1k–2k with concurrent 80 sessions produced stable p99 ~1.7s before fix, 180–250ms after fix.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Canary configuration: disabled cross-process CUDA IPC handoff (feature flag: ipc_handoff_enabled=false) causing model runner to use a single-process pinned allocation for in-flight requests. Canary showed immediate p99 reduction.
- Increased per-process FD limit on dedicated nodes from 4096 -> 16384 (hotfix to cgroup/profile). PR #1289 deployed to infra image.
- Temporary autoscale of dedicated pool to spread customer sessions and avoid hot handoff bursts.

Hotfix and validation notes: 
Hotfix content (short):
- Code change: Add defensive guard in ipc path so that if a page-migration/backoff is detected (driver-level event/timeout), the handoff aborts cleanly and falls back to a pre-allocated host-copy buffer path that avoids futex busy-wait loops. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1298)
- Ops change: Relax cgroup fd limit; add sysctl tuning recommendation for nodes with GDR-enabled GPUs.

Validation (canary -> rollout):
- Reproducer run: 1k seq, 80 concurrent sessions, 30m window. Results before hotfix: p50 120ms, p95 610ms, p99 1.75s. After hotfix (canary): p50 125ms, p95 160ms, p99 230ms.
- nsys traces: show the removal of the 10–50ms futex-kernel gap.
- Customer-sim: acme-fin traffic replayed against canary routing; customer reported latency back within SLA for critical routes.
- Rollout: gradual over 4 hours, monitoring for regressions. No significant regressions observed.

Customer communication:
- Sent initial escalation update to acme-fin and streamly at 2026-04-12 09:10 UTC (private RCA, mitigation status).
- Customer ask: permanent mitigation and assurance for multi-process runtime. Agreed deliverables: enhanced alerting, a short-term config toggle to force single-process mode, longer-term fix in runtime.

Follow-ups and action items (owner -> due):
- (Evan) Merge PR #1298 and coordinate rollback tests on staging (2026-04-16).
- (Priya) Add metric: ipc_handle_open_count and ipc_handle_fallback_rate to per-node telemetry + dashboard (2026-04-19).
- (Marco) Add unit+integration tests that exercise page-migration fallback by mocking driver errors; add to nightly (2026-04-22).
- (Aisha) Update Dedicated node ops runbook: recommended FD and sysctl settings for GDR-enabled nodes (2026-04-18).
- (SRE) Create alert rule: if ipc_handle_fallback_rate > 0.5% over 1m AND p99 > baseline*2 => page-migration-warroom tag (2026-04-20).

Longer-term engineering work (strategic):
- Explore redesign for avoiding cross-process IPC for warmed KV cache: centralized shared daemon vs pinning model runner per-nodet (trade-offs). (Spike assigned to research team, 2 wks).
- Work with infra to validate driver versions and test matrix; vendor engagement for page-migration behavior on GDR-enabled drivers.
- Performance benchmark: expand nightly perf jobs to include high-seq-length multi-process scenarios to catch regressions earlier.

Open questions / unknowns: 
- Why page migration frequency increased for these particular nodes during the burst — possible interaction with kernel memory allocator and CUDA driver heuristics. Need vendor debug symbols to fully trace migration cause.
- Is there any additional corner-case with other models or lower sequence lengths? Initial sampling shows limited occurrence below 512 seq but not fully exhaustive.

Appendix (commands and reproducible steps):
- Reproducer script (internal): scripts/reproducers/ipc_handoff_repro.py --model gpt-xxx-32k --seq 1024 --concurrency 80 --duration 1800
- Profiling notes: nsys profile --output=ipc-capture --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=10ms --target-process <runner-pid>
- Quick check on node: sudo cat /proc/sys/fs/file-nr; sudo prlimit --pid <pid> --nofile; dmesg | grep -i 'page migration'

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc collects the working notes and initial analysis; we should consolidate a polished RCA for customers and legal if requested.
- The change to cgroup limits has been rolled back to conservative values and will be applied via the standard infra release process after additional validation.

Status: in_review — will update with final sign-off and links to merged PRs and post-rollout dashboards.

Attachments / traces: list of trace ids and hostnames included in linked_artifacts above.
